Monsanto Sued by San Diego for Dumping Carcinogenic Chemicals

From Natural Society:

It seems that Monsanto has been dumping banned, carcinogenic chemicals in the bay, and the city of San Diego isn’t too happy about it.

The city of San Diego and the San Diego Unified Port District filed a lawsuit on Monday against the biotech giant Monsanto, accusing the company for polluting the city’s bay for more than 30 years with a carcinogenic chemical that was long ago banned due to its abhorrent affects on human health.

The chemicals in question are Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs). According to a report published by Food & Water Watch, the biotech bully is responsible for creating more than 99% of this dangerous chemical.

It has been found in the bay’s sediments, the water, and in the tissues of multiple forms of aquatic life including in fish and lobster sampled from the bay.

From the March 16 complaint:

“PCBs manufactured by Monsanto have been found in Bay sediments and water and have been identified in tissues of fish, lobsters, and other marine life in the Bay. PCB contamination in and around the Bay affects all San Diegans and visitors who enjoy the Bay, who reasonably would be disturbed by the presence of a hazardous, banned substance in the sediment, water, and wildlife.

“PCBs were not only a substantial factor in causing the City and Port District to incur damages, but a primary driving force behind the need to clean up and abate Bay sediments. In addition, fish consumption warnings are posted at locations in and around Bay tidelands warning the public that fish within the Bay may contain contaminants and directing consumption limitations.”

Related: Monsanto’s Leftover Chemicals Poisoning Ft. McClellan Military Base

The San Diego Reader notes one of the charges put forth by the city of San Diego, stating how Monsanto continued to try and protect its profits while prolonging the use of PCB compounds – even in the face of PCB risks.

PCBs are named under the Toxic Substances Control Act by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and have specific storage and disposal requirements – none of which include dumping the chemicals in San Diego’s waterways.

This toxic substance is heavier than water and can easily be absorbed, even into microorganisms, though Monsanto would like us to believe otherwise.

The EPA’s own review of PCBs stated clearly that:

“There is clear evidence that PCBs cause cancer in animals.”

“An industry scientist commented that ‘all significant studies have been reviewed and are fairly represented in the document.”

“The literature presents overwhelming evidence that PCBs cause cancer in animals.”

“An industry-sponsored peer-reviewed rat study characterized as the ‘gold standard study’ by one peer reviewer, demonstrated that every commercial PCB mixture tested caused cancer.”

Monsanto should pay every man, woman, and child in San Diego and the surrounding area for exposing them to extremely high cancer risks as well as devastating marine life and water supplies.

8 player game, and we're playing with plots cards. Team are as such.

Resistance Spies
Dan R. Blade
Matt Jordan

Rob
Tyler

Round 1
Leader: Dan L.
Dan L. reveals the plot card that makes someone reveal their card to someone, and opinion maker which makes someone vote first. I convince him, "Hey! Give me the card that makes me reveal my identity to someone and I'll reveal it to you so you can trust me on this mission." To balance this out he also gives me Opinion Maker. Now keep in mind both him and I are evil so this is my chance to 'reveal my card' while hiding the truth. Now Jordan throws a fit about how he doesn't trust Dan L. and he could lie so after Dan L. gives me the plot card I reveal my card to Jordan. Jordan, faking being a resistance member, says he trusts me and I'm good now. Now I say I trust Jordan and I beg Dan L. to takes us both on the mission. He does.

Team: Dan L., Jordan, Blade (myself)
Result: 2 success, 1 failure
Score: Spies 1 | Resistance 0

Yup, that's right, we had 3 spies on the first mission and we managed not to botch in the turn in and only get 1 fail (turned in by me). Jordan flips shit and starts blaming Dan L. I jump on the bandwagon because I 'trust' Jordan and damn it Dan L. must be the bad guy. At this point everyone trust me and most people trust Jordan... But not entirely.

Round 2
Leader: Blade
I reveal Keeping a Close Eye On You (lets you see the mission card someone turned in) and No Confidence (lets someone immediately reject a vote). Matt 'convinces' me to give No Confidence to Jordan so that way the 'good guys' always have that in their pocket, and I announce that I trust Matt so I give him Keeping a Close Eye On You. Matt advertises that he'll use it on Jordan to test him here.

Team: Blade, Jordan, Matt, Justin
Result: 4 successes
Score: Spies 1 | Resistance 1

As I suspected Matt actually uses Keeping a Close Eye On You on me, but I turned in a success (as everyone did). Everyone is convinced Dan was the bad apple in the first mission now.

Round 3
Leader: Matt
Matt reveals Strong Leader (you can take over leadership of a round before plot cards are drawn) and Overheard Confidence (you may look at the card of 1 person adjacent to you). He gives Strong Leader to Justin (2 seats to his left) and I ask him to give Overheard Confidence to me so I can test him (Matt) so I KNOW if I can trust him or not. I get the card but start having 'second thoughts' and decide to test Dan L. to 'make sure' I can trust him. Now I put on my best performance because by golly I sweaaarr Dan L's card was good, therefore Jordan must have been the bad guy on the first mission and he just said I was good to get my trust! Tricky evil guy.

Team: Dan L., Blade, Matt, Justin
Result: 3 successes, 1 fail
Score: Spies 2 | Resistance 1

What... but... But Dan L. and Blade are good, and we're sure of Matt! Dammit Justin! Damn you to hell!... Or that's how I played it. I sold my performance hard and everyone was convinced they knew 2 of the spies, Justin and Jordan.

Round 4
Leader: Dan R.
Dan R. reveals Take Responsibility (steal a players plot card) and Opinion Maker (you must vote first each round). I convince him to give Take Responsibility to Matt so he can steal Strong Leader from Justin, and he gives Opinion Maker to Jordan. This mission requires 2 fails so Dan R. wants to do some testing.
